title: Geometric Gain Graph: Zero-Token Graph Construction for Multi-Hop RAG
claim: Similarity-only retrievers are homogeneous and graph retrievers drift off-topic; ours balances relevance and novelty to surface distant key evidence.
layout: 2 panels: left 2x2 schematic cartoons, right stacked retrieval result lists for the same query
description: The figure has two parts. A legend across the top defines the icons: retrieved document nodes (circles), key document nodes (circles with a red check), the query node (blue diamond), entity nodes (triangles), a red dashed GeoGain link, and graph entity links (solid lines). The left part is a 2x2 grid of cartoons for NaiveRAG, LightRAG, HippoRAG2 and G³RAG (Ours). Each cartoon is a green oval of topic-related documents with a dashed inner circle around the query. NaiveRAG stays inside the inner circle. LightRAG spreads out into off-topic nodes. HippoRAG2 reaches slightly further. G³RAG reaches the distant key document through a glowing red dashed link. Short captions under each cartoon name the trap and its cost. The right part starts with a boxed multi-hop question. Below it are four color-coded dashed panels, one per method. Each panel holds five document boxes with similarity scores. The G³RAG panel ends with a highlighted, red-outlined, checked 'East Timor' box.
caption: Illustration of RAG challenges. (a) Relying solely on similarity, NaiveRAG falls into a homogenized Similarity Trap. Conversely, LightRAG overemphasizes relational connections, retrieving off-topic documents and entering a Novelty Trap. Constrained by surface similarity, HippoRAG2 lacks sufficient novelty. In contrast, G$^3$RAG maintains adequate novelty through geometric gain while leveraging similarity. (b) Displays the similarity between retrieved documents and the query. NaiveRAG scores excessively high and LightRAG excessively low. Dominated by similarity, HippoRAG2 cannot efficiently discover more distant key documents like G$^3$RAG.
abstract: Existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems struggle with multi-hop reasoning due to a fundamental inability to balance relevance and novelty. Traditional dense retrievers are constrained by surface-level matching, falling into a homogenized "Similarity Trap". Conversely, emerging Graph RAGs attempt to explore novel documents via heuristic entity extraction, but they introduce prohibitive Large Language Model (LLM) overhead and easily drift into off-topic "Novelty Traps". To fundamentally resolve this contradiction, we propose Geometric Gain Graph (G$^3$RAG), the novel zero-token graph construction paradigm for RAG. G$^3$RAG completely discards the expensive heuristic extraction by LLMs, aiming instead to directly quantify the information gain between nodes through the native document feature space. To this end, we designed a concise edge weight criterion, $\cosÎ¸\cdot \sinÎ¸$, which naturally maps the trade-off between relevance and novelty into a geometric measurement of directional consistency and orthogonality in the vector space, thereby driving the token-free topological construction of the graph. Furthermore, we introduce a topological penalty to suppress the excessive connectivity of high-frequency hubs, forcing the transient diffusion process toward long-tail peripheral nodes that carry critical indirect evidence. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, while entirely eliminating LLM token costs during graph construction, G$^3$RAG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art Graph RAG baselines on complex multi-hop QA benchmarks. The code is available at: https://github.com/deeplearning-LI/G3RAG
